docs.title: Cobblemon PokeTrades
docs.text:
Not released yet

PokeTrades has no public download yet. These pages describe the current development build, 0.0.26. Anything not described here is not in the mod yet.

docs.title: Cobblemon PokeTrades
docs.text:
The in-game trade you remember. Someone out in the world will hand over a Pokémon you cannot catch nearby, if you bring them the one they are asking for. The rarer the prize, the harder the ask.

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Not released yet Cobblemon 1.8+

Get started How traders work

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 🤝 Traders who are Cobblemon NPCs: talk to one and a trade screen shows every offer and which of your Pokémon fit.
  • 💎 The rarer the prize, the harder the ask: five tiers, from a plain swap to a legendary that wants perfect IVs or a shiny.
  • 🎲 Each trader is its own: offers are drawn per trader and kept, and each player takes each offer once.
  • 📛 A traded Pokémon is somebody else's: original trainer kept, a fixed nickname, and trade evolutions on arrival.
  • ❗ A marker over a trader's head tells you it still has something for you.
  • 🏘️ Villages trade too: an unemployed villager next to a Cobblemon PC becomes a Pokémon Trader.
  • 💰 More than Pokémon for Pokémon: trade for items, or for money with CobbleDollars.
  • ⚔️ Beat a trainer, then trade with it: with Radical Cobblemon Trainers, what you give joins its team.

docs.title: Get it
docs.text:
Version 0.0.26 Minecraft 1.21.1 Side Server and every player's game Cobblemon 1.8+ — 1.7.x is not supported Fabric Fabric Language Kotlin, Architectury API NeoForge Kotlin for Forge, Architectury API Optional CobbleDollars: traders sell and buy Pokémon for CobbleDollars · Radical Cobblemon Trainers: trainers you beat trade with you, and what you give joins their team · Cobblemon Action Combat: no trading during its real-time fights (0.1.48 or newer)

No public download yet. New here? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: For Mod Authors
docs.text:
PokeTrades has a public API in the package com.shier.poketrades.api, for mods that want to react to trades, add their own ask conditions, make their own entities trade, or pay money offers in their own currency.

Experimental

The API is marked @ApiStatus.Experimental until the mod's 0.3 milestone. Until 1.0.0, a breaking change to it is named in the mod's changelog under the version that makes it.

Everything here runs on the logical server unless it says otherwise. Register from your mod initialiser, on both sides, before datapacks load.

docs.title: Trade events
docs.text:
PokeTradesEvents.TRADE_PRE and TRADE_POST are Cobblemon observables, used like Cobblemon's own events:

PokeTradesEvents.TRADE_PRE.subscribe { event ->
    if (event.trader.id == "mymod:grumpy" && event.player.level().isNight) event.cancel()
}
  • TRADE_PRE runs after every check and before anything moves. Cancelling it refuses the trade with nothing lost; the player reads that it was cancelled.
  • TRADE_POST runs once the trade happened: what changed hands moved, and the offer and the history are written.

Both carry the player, the trader's entity (npc), its TraderDefinition (trader), the OfferDefinition (offer), and the Pokémon on each side: gave is null when the player pays, received when the trader pays. They run for every offer type. A swap of two Pokémon also posts Cobblemon's own TRADE_EVENT_PRE / TRADE_EVENT_POST, with the trader as the other participant, so a mod that already listens to Cobblemon trades sees these too.

docs.title: Ask conditions
docs.text:
AskConditionTypes.register(id, parser) adds a condition a datapack writes in an ask as {"condition": "<id>", ...}. The mod's own conditions (species, form, gender, nature, ability, ivs, level, shiny, ball) are registered the same way, under bare ids; yours goes under your namespace.

AskConditionTypes.register("mymod:max_level") { reader ->
    MaxLevel(reader.int("max", 1..100))
}

data class MaxLevel(val max: Int) : AskCondition {
    override fun matches(facts: PokemonFacts) = facts.level <= max
    override fun describe(): Component = Component.translatable("mymod.condition.max_level", max)
}

A datapack then writes {"condition": "mymod:max_level", "max": 20}.

  • The parser reads its fields through ConditionReader (string, id, int, choice, their opt versions, and json for anything else). A missing or wrong value fails the offer with a message that names the field, and a key no parser asks about is reported as unknown, so read every key your condition has.
  • matches judges a Pokémon from its PokemonFacts: species, forms, gender, nature, ability, IVs, level, shiny and ball. describe is the line the trade screen and /poketrades info show next to the pass or fail mark.
  • A registered condition counts as one condition toward the tier its ask fits.
  • The client reads the offers it is sent with the same registry: a client without your condition leaves the offer off its screen. Register it on both sides.

docs.title: Trader sources
docs.text:
A TraderSource says which entities of one kind trade, and as which trader. The mod's Cobblemon NPCs (cobblemon_poketrades:npc), villagers (cobblemon_poketrades:villager) and, with Radical Cobblemon Trainers, its trainers (cobblemon_poketrades:rct) are all registered sources. Register yours with TraderSources.register(id, source):

object GymLeaders : TraderSource {
    override fun traderOf(entity: Entity) = (entity as? GymLeader)?.let { "mymod:gym_${it.type}" }
    override fun tradersIn(level: ServerLevel, box: AABB) = level.getEntitiesOfClass(GymLeader::class.java, box)
}
  • Your source wires its entity's right-click itself, and calls TraderSources.open(player, entity) from it on the server. That opens the trade screen, or tells the player the trader is closed or has nothing left.
  • tradersIn feeds the markers over traders with an offer left; the mod filters them per player.
  • Each entity rolls its offers from keyOf(entity) (its UUID by default) the first time anyone uses it, and who took which offer is kept under the same key. A source whose entities stand for one character returns the same key for each, so they share their offers.
  • isOpenTo(entity, player) (true by default) hides the trader from a player: no screen, no marker.
  • receive(entity, trader, pokemon) takes a Pokémon traded to a trader whose destination is team; false (the default) discards it.

docs.title: Currencies
docs.text:
A CurrencyProvider pays for money offers: balance, withdraw (false, with nothing taken, when the player has less), deposit, and format, how an amount reads (1,500 ₽). Amounts are whole units. Register it with Currencies.register(id, provider).

Money offers use the first currency registered; with none they are left off every trader. The mod registers CobbleDollars itself when it is installed.

docs.title: Commands & Configuration
docs.text: Everything is under /poketrades. Two commands are for every player; the rest need operator level 2. A trader id written without a namespace is read as cobblemon_poketrades:.

docs.title: For every player
docs.text: Command What it does /poketrades info the trader you look at: each offer, what it asks, and whether you can still take it /poketrades history your last 20 trades, newest first

docs.title: Managing traders
docs.text:
Command What it does /poketrades spawn <trader> place an NPC that trades as <trader> where you stand /poketrades remove remove the trader you look at; its rolled offers and who took them are forgotten /poketrades list every loaded trader, with clickable coordinates (teleport) and UUID (copy) /poketrades reset <player> [trader] [offer] give a player back the offers they took: all of them, one trader's (by UUID), or one offer /poketrades reload reread every trader, pool, category and item value without a full /reload

A broken definition file is skipped whole, with one line in the server log naming the file and the field; everything else still loads. reload says how many errors and warnings there were.

docs.title: Building a trader in game
docs.text:
A trader can live in the world instead of a datapack, built one command at a time, with no JSON to write. Only these traders can be edited by command: a datapack trader belongs to its datapack.

Command What it does /poketrades create <trader> [name] a new, empty trader /poketrades rename <trader> <name> its name, and the name tag of its loaded NPCs /poketrades delete <trader> remove it from the world; a datapack trader with the same id takes over /poketrades export <trader> write it as a datapack into datapacks/poketrades_export/ /poketrades offer add <trader> <offer> <species> <gives> a Pokémon-for-Pokémon offer asking for <species>; <gives> is a Cobblemon Pokémon spec with a level, like eevee level=15 /poketrades offer ask <trader> <offer> <condition> [value] set one condition of its ask /poketrades offer unask <trader> <offer> <condition> clear one /poketrades offer tier <trader> <offer> <1-5> set its tier /poketrades offer remove <trader> <offer> remove it /poketrades offer list <trader> its offers, buckets and nicknames /poketrades nickname add\|remove <trader> <name> the nicknames it gives /poketrades bucket add <trader> <pool> [count] · bucket remove <trader> <pool> draw offers from a pool

A condition's value is written as in a datapack: a species, form, gender, nature, ability or ball id; a level as its minimum; IVs as perfect=N or hp=31,speed=20; shiny takes none. An edit that would break the trader is refused with nothing changed, and the reason in chat.

An exported trader loads from its datapack after /reload, but the world copy keeps precedence until you delete it.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text: Command What it does /poketrades debug category <species> its category, its default tier, and what decided it /poketrades debug roll <trader> [seed] preview the offers a trader would roll, without saving them /poketrades debug give <trader> <offer> hand yourself an offer's Pokémon as a trade would build it /poketrades debug validate check every definition and print each problem, without reloading /poketrades debug state [npc] what the world remembers of the trader you look at, or of one UUID

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Every feature can be switched off or tuned on a live server, and the change is saved at once to config/cobblemon_poketrades.json.

Command What it does /poketrades config <feature> whether it is on, and its settings /poketrades config <feature> enabled <true\|false> switch it on or off /poketrades config <feature> <setting> <value> tune one setting /poketrades config <feature> reset that feature back to its defaults /poketrades config reset_all every feature back to its defaults Feature Setting (default, range) Off means npc_traders no trader opens its screen, shows a marker, answers info or accepts a trade pc_selection an ask is met from the party only; the screen hides the PC nickname_lock a Pokémon a trader gave can be renamed like any other marker range (64, 8–256 blocks) no marker over any trader server_wide_tier min_tier (5, 1–5) every offer is once per player, none once for the whole server history cap (100, 1–1000 trades per player) no trade is written to anyone's history reoffer max_held (6, 1–54) a trader that offers what it receives keeps nothing new; what it holds stays offered battle_guard trades, purchases and sales go through during a Cobblemon battle or an Action Combat fight; a Pokémon on your own battle team is still refused as busy

max_held applies to a trader whose own definition sets no limit.

battle_guard is on by default, so nothing changes unless an operator runs /poketrades config battle_guard enabled false (/poketrades config battle_guard reset brings the block back).

docs.title: Community Credits
docs.text:
PokeTrades is built on the work of others:

  • Cobblemon, whose Pokémon, NPCs, trade screen and trade events every trade goes through.
  • CobbleDollars, the currency of the money offers.
  • Radical Cobblemon Trainers, whose trainers and battle records decide who trades with whom.

Found a bug or have an idea? Post it in the Discord.

docs.title: Datapack Format
docs.text:
Traders, their offers and the numbers behind tiers are JSON files in a datapack. Each kind lives in its own folder under data/<namespace>/poketrades/:

Folder What a file holds traders/ one trader pools/ one pool of offers that traders draw from categories/ which category some species fall in item_values/ what items are worth, for the tier of item offers

A file's id is its namespace and path without .json: data/mypack/poketrades/traders/fisherman.json is the trader mypack:fisherman. The mod's own files use the cobblemon_poketrades namespace; a pack replaces one by shipping a file at the same path. /reload or /poketrades reload picks up changes.

A broken file is skipped whole

A file loads whole or not at all. Its first bad field is one error line in the server log, naming the file and the field (offers[2].asks[0].min), and every other file still loads. A field the format does not have is only a warning, usually a typo. /poketrades debug validate prints every problem without reloading.

Changing a file never changes the offers a trader already rolled: those are kept for good.

docs.title: Traders
docs.text:
{
  "name": "Trader Wilma",
  "nicknames": ["Abby", "Pip", "Clover"],
  "destination": "discard",
  "offers": ["cobblemon_poketrades:o03"],
  "buckets": [
    { "pool": "common_pfp_t1", "count": 2 },
    { "pool": "uncommon_pfp_t2", "count": 1 }
  ]
}
Field Required What it is name yes the name shown on the screen and in chat nicknames no the names a Pokémon it gives can get, one at random; empty or missing, it keeps its species name destination no where a Pokémon it receives goes: discard (default), reoffer or team (Where your Pokémon goes) reoffer_limit no how many received Pokémon a reoffer trader holds at once (1 or more); missing, the server's reoffer max_held (6) offers no fixed offers, each written in full (Offers) or as the id of an offer some pool defines buckets no each { "pool": <pool id>, "count": <1 or more> }: draw that many offers from that pool
  • A trader needs at least one fixed offer or bucket.
  • A pool id without a namespace is a pool of the trader's own namespace.
  • A trader never draws the same offer twice, and never draws one it already holds as fixed. Its buckets cannot ask a pool for more offers than it has left once the trader's fixed offers and earlier buckets are taken out.
  • A trader whose bucket names a pool that did not load is skipped too, with its own error line.

To make an NPC trade as this trader, see Cobblemon NPCs. An RCT trainer uses the trader rct/<trainer id> (RCT trainers), and the village trader is cobblemon_poketrades:villager.

docs.title: Pools
docs.text:
A pool is a list of offers that share one trade type and one tier, so a trader can say "two common swaps" without naming them.

{
  "category": "common",
  "type": "pokemon_for_pokemon",
  "tier": 1,
  "offers": [
    {
      "id": "mypack:wooper_for_psyduck",
      "gives": "wooper level=12",
      "asks": [{ "condition": "species", "species": "psyduck" }]
    }
  ]
}
Field Required What it is type yes the offer type of every offer in it category no the category its offers trade: common, uncommon, rare, baby, fossil, starter, paradox, ultra_beast, legendary, mythical tier no 1 to 5; missing, the category's tier. One of the two must be there offers yes at least one offer

An offer in a pool takes the pool's type and tier. It may write them again, but only with the same values.

docs.title: Offers
docs.text: Field Required What it is id yes unique across everything loaded, like mypack:wooper_for_psyduck type outside a pool the offer type tier no 1 to 5; see How an offer gets its tier gives yes what the trader hands over asks yes what it takes

docs.title: Offer types
docs.text:
type gives asks pokemon_for_pokemon a Pokémon a Pokémon ask pokemon_for_items a Pokémon items pokemon_for_money a Pokémon money buy_with_items items a Pokémon ask buy_with_money money a Pokémon ask
  • A Pokémon is a Cobblemon Pokémon properties string, as in /pokegive, and it must set a level: "eevee level=15", "vulpix form=alola level=20 nature=timid". Whatever it leaves out rolls like a wild Pokémon of that level, except that it is never shiny and comes in a Poké Ball unless the string says so (shiny=yes, pokeball=ultra_ball).
  • Items is a list of { "item": "minecraft:emerald", "count": 8 }, at least one; count is 1 when missing. An item counts by id alone.
  • Money is a whole number, 1 or more, in units of the currency (CobbleDollars): "gives": 400.
  • A Pokémon ask is a list of conditions, at least one.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
Each condition is an object with a condition field and the fields of that condition. An ask lists each condition at most once, and a Pokémon must meet all of them. An id without a namespace is Cobblemon's.

condition Fields Example species species { "condition": "species", "species": "psyduck" } form form, any case { "condition": "form", "form": "alola" } gender gender: male, female or genderless { "condition": "gender", "gender": "female" } nature nature; a mint counts { "condition": "nature", "nature": "timid" } ability ability { "condition": "ability", "ability": "drizzle" } ivs min: the least IV per stat (0 to 31), or perfect: how many stats at 31 (1 to 6) { "condition": "ivs", "min": { "hp": 31, "speed": 20 } } level min, 1 or more { "condition": "level", "min": 30 } shiny none { "condition": "shiny" } ball ball { "condition": "ball", "ball": "ultra_ball" }

The stats of ivs are hp, attack, defence, special_attack, special_defence and speed. A Bottle Cap counts. Other mods add conditions under their own namespace (For Mod Authors).

docs.title: How an offer gets its tier
docs.text:
The first of these that applies:

  1. the offer's own tier;
  2. its pool's tier (or its pool's category's);
  3. for an item offer, what its items are worth (Item values); if one of them has no value, the offer must set its tier, or it fails;
  4. for a money offer, its price (the price bands);
  5. for a fixed Pokémon-for-Pokémon offer, the category of the species it gives, worked out when the trader rolls.

The tier tables guide balance; they do not bind it. A Pokémon-for-Pokémon ask that does not fit its tier, items worth another tier's band, or a price in another band, is a warning, and the offer loads anyway.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
Every species already has a category, from its Cobblemon labels or its catch rate (Tiers). A file in categories/ sets it by hand:

{
  "species": {
    "eevee": "rare",
    "othermod:fluffle": "legendary"
  }
}

A species without a namespace is Cobblemon's. Files are read in id order, and when two set the same species, the first one keeps it and the second gets a warning.

docs.title: Item values
docs.text:
What items are worth, in emeralds, for the tier of item offers:

{
  "values": {
    "minecraft:emerald": 1,
    "cobblemon:fire_stone": 12,
    "cobblemon:master_ball": 250
  }
}

An item without a namespace is Minecraft's, and a value is a whole number, 0 or more. The mod ships values for 37 items (Poké Balls, evolution stones, held items, the Master Ball…) in cobblemon_poketrades:default. Any other pack's value for the same item replaces the mod's.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: PokeTrades targets Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric and NeoForge, with Cobblemon 1.8. Cobblemon 1.7.x is not supported.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Notes Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric Loader or NeoForge the jar for your loader Fabric Language Kotlin or Kotlin for Forge the one for your loader Architectury API both loaders Cobblemon 1.8

Optional, each adding something when it is there:

  • CobbleDollars: traders sell Pokémon for CobbleDollars and buy yours (Offer types). Without it, money offers stay off every trader.
  • Radical Cobblemon Trainers: a trainer you beat trades with you, and what you give it joins its team (RCT trainers).
  • Cobblemon Action Combat 0.1.48 or newer: trades, purchases and sales are refused during its real-time fights, as they are during a Cobblemon battle (unless an operator turns battle_guard off). Without it nothing changes.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Cobblemon and the libraries for your loader.
  2. Drop the PokeTrades jar for your loader into mods/. Never put both loaders' jars in.
  3. On a server, install it on the server and on every player's game. A trader's NPC data is sent to each client, and a client without the mod cannot join.
  4. Find a trader. Out of the box that is a villager working at a Cobblemon PC in a village, or one of the sample traders an operator places with /poketrades spawn.
  5. Right-click it: the trade screen opens.

Removing the mod

Taking PokeTrades out of a world breaks every NPC that still uses its trade interaction: Cobblemon cannot read it back. Remove those NPCs first (/poketrades remove).

docs.title: The sample traders
docs.text:
Four traders ship with the mod. An operator places any of them with /poketrades spawn <trader>:

Trader Id Trades Trader Wilma wilma common to rare Pokémon, a money sale and a money purchase Professor Ines ines starters, fossils, a baby, an item sale and a starter for money; keeps what you give for the next player Keeper Soren soren legendaries, a mythical, a paradox Pokémon and a legendary for money; tier-5 offers are once for the whole server Trader Bram bram items and money only, and always buys a shiny Magikarp for a Master Ball; keeps what you give for the next player

The village trader is a fifth one, villager. A modpack replaces or empties any of them with its own datapack (Datapack Format).

docs.title: Traders
docs.text: A trader is someone in the world who swaps Pokémon with you. Right-click one and its trade screen opens: its offers on the right, your party on the left, and, under the two portraits, every condition of the offer with a mark for whether your Pokémon meets it.

docs.title: Who trades
docs.text: Three kinds of entity can be a trader. Each one trades as a trader definition, which says its name, its nicknames and where its offers come from. The definitions come from datapacks (Datapack Format), or are built in game by an operator (Commands).

docs.title: Cobblemon NPCs
docs.text:
Any Cobblemon NPC trades when its interaction names a trader. That works on an NPC class, a preset or a single NPC, however it got into the world: placed with Cobblemon's NPC tools, spawned by a structure, or placed with /poketrades spawn <trader>, which also dresses it in the trader's white coat.

{
  "names": ["Trader Wilma"],
  "interaction": {
    "type": "cobblemon_poketrades:trade",
    "trader": "wilma"
  }
}

A trader id without a namespace is read as cobblemon_poketrades:. An id no datapack loads does nothing on click, and the server log says so once.

docs.title: Village traders
docs.text: An unemployed villager next to a Cobblemon PC takes the Pokémon Trader profession, with an open coat over its village's own clothes (and a worn version once zombified). Its right-click always opens the trade screen, never the vanilla one. It trades as the villager trader: by default five offers from the common, uncommon and item pools. It never levels up, and breaking its PC makes it lose the profession.

docs.title: RCT trainers
docs.text:
With Radical Cobblemon Trainers installed, a trainer trades once you have beaten it, by RCT's own record of who beat whom, and from then on for good. Everyone who has not beaten it still gets the battle. When the battle ends, the trainer tells you its right-click trades now.

A trainer carries offers when a trader named rct/<trainer id> is loaded, for example data/cobblemon_poketrades/poketrades/traders/rct/leader_brock.json. Every copy of that trainer offers the same, and each player takes each offer once.

docs.title: Offers
docs.text:
A trader holds fixed offers, which it always has, and buckets, each drawing a number of offers at random from an offer pool. The draw happens once, the first time anyone uses that trader, and is kept for good: a reload or a changed datapack never rerolls it. Two NPCs built from the same structure roll apart.

Each offer can be taken once per player per trader. From tier 5 (by default) an offer is once for the whole server: the first player to take it claims it, and everyone else sees it locked as taken by another player. An operator changes that tier, or switches it off, with server_wide_tier.

docs.title: Offer types
docs.text:
Type The trader gives It asks for Pokémon for Pokémon a Pokémon a Pokémon that meets its conditions Pokémon for items a Pokémon items Pokémon for money a Pokémon money Buy with items items a Pokémon that meets its conditions Buy with money money a Pokémon that meets its conditions
  • Items count by id alone: any emerald is an emerald, whatever its name or enchantments. Your whole inventory counts, offhand and armour included. The screen shows how many of each you carry. Items a trader pays that do not fit in your inventory drop at your feet.
  • Money needs a currency. With CobbleDollars installed the price leaves your balance, or the payment lands in it, only when the server confirms the trade. Without a currency, money offers are left off every trader and the server log says so once.

docs.title: What an ask can require
docs.text:
The Pokémon a trader asks for is a list of conditions, and your Pokémon must meet all of them:

Condition Met when your Pokémon… species is that species form is in that form (alola, galar…) gender is male, female or genderless nature has that nature; a mint counts ability has that ability IVs has at least the IVs asked per stat, or that many perfect (31) IVs; a Bottle Cap counts level is at least that level shiny is shiny ball was caught in that ball

How each is written: Conditions. Other mods can add conditions of their own (For Mod Authors).

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
Every offer has a tier from 1 to 5. In a Pokémon-for-Pokémon offer the tier follows how rare the Pokémon the trader gives is, and says how much the ask carries:

Tier Gives a Pokémon that is… The ask carries 1 common the species only 2 uncommon + 1 condition 3 rare, baby or fossil + 2 conditions 4 starter or paradox + 3 conditions, or a minimum IV 5 legendary, mythical or Ultra Beast perfect IVs, or shiny

A species' category comes from its own Cobblemon labels first (mythical, legendary, Ultra Beast, paradox, starter, fossil, baby); a species with none of them is common with a catch rate of 120 or more, rare at 45 or less, and uncommon in between. Pokémon from other mods follow the same rule, and a datapack can set the category of any species. An operator checks one with /poketrades debug category <species>.

For item offers the tier is what the items are worth, counted in emeralds:

Worth up to 10 up to 30 up to 80 up to 200 above 200 Tier 1 2 3 4 5

For money offers it is the price:

Price up to 2,500 up to 10,000 up to 40,000 up to 120,000 above 120,000 Tier 1 2 3 4 5

A trader pays about a quarter of what it sells a Pokémon for.

docs.title: The trade screen
docs.text:
• The trader's offers fill the right grid, six to a page. An offer you already took, or a once-per-server one another player claimed, stays on the grid locked and says why.
  • Your party fills the left grid. A Pokémon that misses the ask carries a lock but can still be picked, so the marks show what it lacks.
  • PC opens your boxes one at a time, with how many Pokémon in each box match. A Pokémon in your PC can be traded like one in your party (unless the server switched pc_selection off).
  • Press Trade. The server checks everything again: that the trader is within 8 blocks, the offer is still yours to take, and the Pokémon is still yours and meets the ask. A chat line says what you traded, and the screen opens again with that offer locked as taken.

A trade happens whole or not at all. You cannot trade while in a battle (a Cobblemon battle, or a Cobblemon Action Combat fight with Action Combat 0.1.48 or newer), nor a Pokémon tethered to a pasture. An operator can switch the battle block off with battle_guard: trades then go through mid-battle, but a Pokémon on your own battle team is still refused as busy. A Pokémon you sent out goes back to its ball first. Leaving the game mid-trade, pressing twice, or two players confirming the same once-per-server offer at the same moment never moves a Pokémon that should not move. With a full party the Pokémon you receive goes to your PC, and with a full party and PC it takes the slot your Pokémon leaves.

docs.title: The Pokémon you receive
docs.text:
• It comes out like a wild Pokémon of its level, with whatever the offer does not fix (IVs, nature, gender, ability, moves…) rolled as a spawn would. It is never shiny and comes in a Poké Ball, unless the offer says otherwise.
  • The trader is its original trainer, and it carries a nickname from the trader's list (or its species name when the list is empty). That nickname cannot be changed: renaming it snaps back, and a name tag on it fails without being used up.
  • It arrives as from any Cobblemon trade: its friendship starts at its species' base value, a Pokémon that evolves by trading (Kadabra, Haunter, Machoke…) offers its evolution right away, and the trade counts for Cobblemon's trade advancements and statistic.

docs.title: Where your Pokémon goes
docs.text:
Each trader decides what happens to the Pokémon you give it:

  • Gone (the default): only your trade history remembers it.
  • Offered to the next players: the trader holds it, six at a time by default, the oldest leaving first. Other players see it as you gave it, with you as its original trainer and your nickname, which they can change. You never see your own Pokémon offered back, and each one can be traded once. Its ask is borrowed from the trader pools of its own category and tier.
  • Joins the trainer's team, for an RCT trainer: it is added to that trainer's battle team, six at most. The trainer's own members always stay, the oldest traded one leaves to make room, and every player meets the same team.

docs.title: The marker
docs.text: A trader that still holds an offer you can take carries Cobblemon's trade icon over its head, on every trader within 64 blocks. Once you have taken all its offers the marker goes away for you, while other players still see theirs. A once-per-server offer another player claims takes the marker away for everyone it was the last offer for.

docs.title: Looking a trader up
docs.text:
• /poketrades info, looking at a trader: each offer, what it gives, every condition or item of its ask, and whether you can still take it.
  • /poketrades history: the trades you made, newest first.

Neither says where a trader stands: finding one is part of the game.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: I can't join the server
docs.text: The server runs PokeTrades and your game does not. Install it on your game too: a trader's NPC data is sent to every client, and a client without the mod cannot read it.

docs.title: Right-clicking a trader does nothing
docs.text: Its interaction names a trader no datapack loads: the server log says which, once. If the line above the hotbar says the trader is not trading on this server, an operator switched npc_traders off. If it says it has nothing to trade right now, you have taken every offer it has for you.

docs.title: An RCT trainer battles me instead of trading
docs.text: You have not beaten that trainer yet, by RCT's own record. Beat it once and its right-click trades from then on.

docs.title: A trader has no money offers
docs.text: Money offers need a currency: install CobbleDollars. Without it they are left off every trader, and the server log says so once.

docs.title: I can't pick a Pokémon from my PC
docs.text: The server switched pc_selection off: asks are met from the party only.

docs.title: The trade was refused
docs.text: The server checks everything again when you press Trade. It refuses when you are in a battle (a Cobblemon battle or, with Action Combat 0.1.48 or newer, one of its real-time fights: trade once it is over; an operator can switch this block off with battle_guard, but a Pokémon on your own battle team is then still refused as busy), the Pokémon is tethered to a pasture, you walked more than 8 blocks from the trader, or another player just claimed that once-per-server offer. Nothing changes hands when a trade is refused.

docs.title: I can't rename a Pokémon I got in a trade
docs.text: That is the nickname lock: a Pokémon a trader gave keeps the name the trader gave it. An operator can switch nickname_lock off.

docs.title: My datapack trader doesn't show up
docs.text: Run /poketrades debug validate: it prints every problem in every file, naming the file and the field. A file with an error is skipped whole; an unknown field is only a warning.
